derivation: For odd n, floor(n^2/4)=(n^2-1)/4 and e=(n^2+3)/4.
For every integer |B|, S_m has nonzero sqrt(3) coefficient -n/4, hence is irrational.
A finite unweighted set has integer cardinality, so it cannot have cardinality exactly S_m.
M809C-05.scope: This does not refute weighted nonnegative atoms of total mass S_m or an integer floor/ceiling ledger with an explicit rounding term.

M809C-08.proof: I_mix counts distinct mixed colours. Choosing each colour's unique high internal anchor is injective by colour, and the inherited rich-outer theorem places all selected high edges in one pairwise-C7-compatible family. Since I_mix is integral, I_mix>=ceil(Phi) supplies at least Phi compatible edges of distinct colours.
M809C-08.boundary: The profile verifies that the scalar identity plus R_A>S_m does not force either displayed channel to reach Phi. It is not a graph-realizable counterexample and therefore does not refute a future cross-channel compatibility theorem.

M809C-11.statement: For a finite demand-to-carrier bipartite graph, the minimum number unpaid is |D|-nu=max_T(|T|-|N(T)|). Full payment is equivalent to every Hall inequality |N(T)|>=|T|.
M809C-11.proof_boundary: The lower bound follows because at most |N(T)| members of T can be matched. For the upper bound, adjoin delta=max_T(|T|-|N(T)|) universal dummy carriers, apply Hall, and delete the dummy carriers.
M809C-11.scope: Hall allocates already constructed typed carriers along already proved legal arcs. It does not construct carriers, arcs, ownership maps, or graph-specific expansion.
